### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**3** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 64807a9c0e9e07d67758ac82578d1c1dd0bc7484` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `30f76c1a1c464e567e5cd7aae7677c1c2f197701` — the merge of head `8284267774a4c24ba8627951ea128e64e263c20a` into base `64807a9c0e9e07d67758ac82578d1c1dd0bc7484`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 30f76c1a1c464e567e5cd7aae7677c1c2f197701 && git checkout 30f76c1a1c464e567e5cd7aae7677c1c2f197701
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 64807a9c0e9e07d67758ac82578d1c1dd0bc7484 8284267774a4c24ba8627951ea128e64e263c20a && git checkout -B drift-repro 64807a9c0e9e07d67758ac82578d1c1dd0bc7484 && git merge --no-ff 8284267774a4c24ba8627951ea128e64e263c20a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 64807a9c0e9e07d67758ac82578d1c1dd0bc7484
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Review — FAIL

Head-sha: `f1706ea9254dfc848f99f63ee1f39cef43d2c7b4`
Reviewer: review-a (areas S1 + S3) · read 2026-11-15T13:55Z · diff read against the merge's main parent `45dee177` (6 files, +110/−31, matches the PR files list)
Implemented-by: session_01QsR2jTEivi2wogPpeo3xd5 (area S3 dispatch) · Reviewed-by: session_01QsR2jTjrNnh6b2BkCXFugM

**What holds**

- The premise holds: `NAMESPACE_SCOPED_BARE_NAME_TYPES` (`@objectstack/core`) lists all 13 covered types at this head. So the old one-name-per-deployment reason was false for the ordinary case, a refusal within one namespace or beside a package with no namespace.
- Area point 2 is accepted. The per-deployment branch is the card's ruling and core's documented path for a type that joins the covered list before it narrows. A `vi.doMock` pin is the honest way to hold an unreachable-today branch, and the mixed-list order is pinned.
- Area point 4 is accepted. `hook-binder.ts` is a comment-only change, and the comment is true. `bindAppArtifactHandlers` (`packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts`) catches the throw per owner group and logs `Failed to bind declarative hooks` at `error`.
- The ablation is accepted, and so is the account of the discarded first ablation. `Clause-②: no` / `Metadata-protocol: none` is right, because no refusal moves and the code and status are unchanged.

**Must-fix**

1. **The new sentence is false for the two refusals that cross namespaces (area point 3, and one more).** Under a narrowed type, two holdings still meet whatever their namespaces (`bareNameHoldersMeet`, and the module docblock at `bare-name-one-holder.ts` ~225):
   - a name the platform requests by its bare spelling (`PLATFORM_REQUESTED_BARE_NAMES_BY_TYPE`: `email_template`'s `auth.password_reset`, `auth.verify_email`, `auth.magic_link`, `auth.invitation`, …), which keeps one holder per deployment;
   - a bundle addition (`isBundleAdditionPair`), which is refused as before.

   In both cases the conflict line names two holders of different namespaces. The reason then says "a package of another namespace may ship the same name", which contradicts the refusal it explains. For the `auth.*` mails the old sentence (one per deployment) was true, so this PR turns a true reason into a false one. That case is also the likeliest real conflict, two packages both overriding a platform mail. It is the same defect #33507 fixes, introduced for these two refusals.

   Fix, your choice of route:
   - (a) In `bare-name-one-holder.ts` alone: when the narrowed group includes a type with such exceptions (today `email_template`), the narrowed sentence names them. For example: "…except a name the platform requests by its bare spelling (the `auth.*` mails) and a member a dependent package adds under its base's name, which keep one holder whatever the namespace."
   - (b) Pass the conflicts, not only their types, from `bareNameReasonFor` (`registry.ts`, a claim amendment), so each refusal gets the sentence for the rule that fired.

   Either way, pin a cross-namespace refusal of a platform-requested `auth.*` template and of a bundle addition (the flow-family file has the bundle fixture at ~720). Assert that the reason does not claim another namespace may ship the name, and ablate the new clause.

**Nits (no re-review needed)**

2. `CONSUMER_CLAUSE` is now reachable only through the mocked branch. Keeping it is right for the same reason as point 2. Its docblock already says so.

**Gates:** not judged. At review time 19 check-runs were in progress, 13 success, 16 skipped, none red.

Next: a new head with item 1. I review the delta only.
